answer.evidence: The shelf is drawn face-on. The silhouette is a flat 30px-wide rectangle from row 4 to row 30, with only a 1-2 row frame rim at rows 3-4 and no top band or ellipse. The compartments are vertical interior faces separated by shelf-board edges (rows 11, 22) with dark shadow bands below them (rows 12-13, 23-24). These boards are read as parts of the front face and do not form a receding top surface. The items on top at rows 1-5 are decor. The result is a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden shelf holding small goods. Its measured facts are on par with the references: 17 visible tones per tile, matching the cheese stall (17) and close to the well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline carries a tint. By eye the outline is dark brown beside the wood, not a black sticker line. The wood frame shows about 4 steps with a lighter top edge and darker shelf interiors. The shelf items (books, boxes, cloth) add varied small shapes and clusters. It has less grain and per-plank highlights than the stall's and well's wood, and the frame reads a bit uniform. At this scale it would sit acceptably next to the references, though marginally thinner in material ramps than the stall or well.

styleAnswer.evidence: The shelf is a wooden frame with a dark brown, tinted outline beside the wood and a darker recessed interior. Goods on the shelves (folded cloth, boxes, bottles) break up the surface. The measured facts support it. None of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is tinted rather than a black sticker line. Its 28 total colours are below the stall (40) and well (38). The wood ramp is about 4 steps against the references' 5-6, and the plank grain is a little sparse. A careful artist would still accept it next to the references without it looking flatter or thinner.
